title: Do not get dragged into disputes; keep inviting to your Lord.
subtitle: Every nation had its rites; stay on the straight path
then: Ibn Jarir said every prophet's nation had its rites. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}do not let their dispute divert you from the truth{/idea}. Invite them to your Lord, for you are on a clear and straight path.
now: Someone in the comments wants to fight about your faith for the hundredth time. You could spend your whole evening replying. {idea}The verse says: do not get dragged in; keep calling kindly{/idea}, and keep walking your path.
old: If I do not win the argument, I have failed my faith.
new: My role is to invite and stay steady, not to win every dispute.
try: Leave one argument unanswered today and spend that time on your own worship.

title: If they keep arguing: Allah knows best what you do.
subtitle: A calm reply that ends the circle
then: Ibn Kathir compares this to the verse: for me are my deeds and for you yours. He calls it {trap}a stern warning{/trap} to those arguing, since Allah knows their deeds, and enough is He as witness.
now: Your brother has argued the same point at every family dinner for two years. You feel the heat rising. {idea}One calm sentence can close it: Allah knows best what each of us does.{/idea}
old: I have to keep arguing until they admit I am right.
new: When arguing goes nowhere, I can hand it to Allah who knows everything.
try: Use the phrase Allah knows best in one tense conversation today, sincerely.

title: Allah will judge on the Day what you differed about.
subtitle: Disagreements have a final hearing
then: Ibn Kathir pairs it with the command to {idea}invite, stand firm, and not follow their desires{/idea}. The disputes the Prophet ﷺ faced did not need to be resolved in the moment; Allah would judge them.
now: There is an old family disagreement that never got resolved, and it keeps you up. {reward}The verse lifts the weight: not every difference must be settled by you, now.{/reward}
old: Every disagreement I have must be resolved in this life.
new: Some differences wait for Allah's judgment; I can live in peace meanwhile.
try: Make peace in your heart with one unresolved disagreement by leaving it with Allah.

title: Everything in heaven and earth is known and recorded.
subtitle: And for Allah that is easy
then: Ibn Kathir says not even a speck of dust escapes His knowledge, and He {idea}wrote everything before it happened{/idea}. He cites the Prophet ﷺ: the first thing Allah created was the Pen, and it wrote what will happen until the Day.
now: You forget passwords, appointments, where you parked. You worry your quiet sacrifices are forgotten too. {reward}The verse says every one of them is written{/reward}, and keeping it all is easy for Him.
old: My small good deeds slip by unnoticed.
new: Everything is known and written, and it costs Allah nothing to keep it.
try: Do one small kindness today, trusting it is written even if no one sees.

title: Worship with no proof, only habit handed down.
subtitle: No authority, no knowledge, no helper
then: Ibn Kathir says it was {trap}handed down from their fathers and ancestors with no evidence{/trap}, and Shaytan made it attractive. The listeners in Makkah defended old ways simply because they were old.
now: Your family has always done a certain ritual at weddings or funerals, and no one knows where it comes from. Questioning it feels rude. {idea}The verse asks: what is the proof?{/idea} Habit is not authority.
old: If my family has always done it, it must be right.
new: What I do in worship should rest on proof from Allah, not just habit.
try: Pick one religious habit you have and find its source this week.

title: Their faces darken when the clear verses are recited.
subtitle: Anger at the message, and something worse
then: Ibn Kathir says when proofs for Tawhid were mentioned, they {trap}nearly attacked those who recited{/trap}, harming them with tongue and hand. The Prophet ﷺ was told to answer: what awaits you is worse than what you threaten.
now: Someone shares a verse in the group chat and you feel irritation before you have read it. Your face tightens. {idea}The verse asks you to notice that reaction in yourself{/idea}, and to soften instead of push back.
old: When I am reminded of faith, it is fair to feel annoyed.
new: Irritation at a clear reminder is a warning sign in my own heart.
try: The next reminder you receive today, read it twice and reply with thanks.

title: All their gods together could not create one fly.
subtitle: Nor take back what a fly steals
then: Ibn Kathir says listen means {idea}pay attention and understand{/idea}. Even if every idol joined forces they could not make a single fly, nor take back what it snatches. Ibn Abbas said the seeker is the idol and the sought is the fly.
now: A fly lands on your plate, you swat, it escapes, and you cannot get back the crumb it took. {idea}Now think of whatever you are treating as all-powerful{/idea}: money, status, a person. Could it make even this fly?
old: Some things in my life are strong enough to rely on completely.
new: Anything besides Allah is weaker than it looks; it cannot make a fly.
try: Next time a fly bothers you today, let it remind you who alone creates.

title: They did not value Allah as He deserves.
subtitle: The root of every false worship
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}did not recognize the might and power of Allah{/trap} when they worshipped beside Him things that cannot ward off a fly. He is the All-Strong who created everything, and none can resist Him.
now: You pray quickly, distracted, while your mind is on a client call. You would never treat a visiting dignitary like that. {idea}The verse asks: how big is Allah in your day?{/idea}
old: Allah is one part of my life among many.
new: Allah is the All-Strong; my day should reflect His greatness.
try: Before your next prayer, pause for ten seconds and remember who you are standing before.

title: Allah chooses messengers from angels and from people.
subtitle: He knows who deserves to carry His message

row.title: Allah
sub: knows best where to place it

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}chooses messengers as He wills{/idea}, from angels and from humans. He hears what His servants say and sees who deserves it, as in: Allah knows best with whom to place His message.
now: You see someone quiet and unremarkable at work turn out to be the one everyone trusts. {idea}Allah's choices are not based on what impresses us.{/idea} He sees what we do not.
old: The most impressive people must be the most chosen.
new: Allah chooses by what He sees and hears, not by what impresses people.
try: Notice one overlooked person today and treat them with real respect.

title: He knows what is before them and after them.
subtitle: The messengers are guarded; all matters return to Him
then: Ibn Kathir says none of the messengers' affairs are hidden from Him; {reward}He is guarding them{/reward}, witness to what is said about them, protecting and supporting them, as when the Prophet ﷺ was told Allah would protect him from people.
now: You are carrying something heavy for someone else: a sick parent, a younger sibling, a team at work. You worry about what comes next. {reward}The One who knows past and future also guards those who carry His trust.{/reward}
old: I have to figure out every future step alone.
new: Allah knows what is ahead and behind me, and every matter returns to Him.
try: Hand one worry about the future to Allah in a short dua before bed.

title: Bow, prostrate, worship, do good, and you may succeed.
subtitle: The surah's second verse of prostration
then: Ibn Kathir records the Prophet ﷺ saying Surat Al-Hajj was blessed with {reward}two prostrations{/reward}; this is the second. After the whole surah's arguments and parables, the believers are given simple actions.
now: You read success stories on your commute: the founder, the athlete, the influencer. Then you get home tired. {idea}The verse gives a different definition: bow, prostrate, worship, and do good.{/idea}
old: Success means getting ahead in the world.
new: Success, as Allah defines it, starts on the prayer mat and shows in good deeds.
try: Pray your next prayer slowly and do one good deed straight after it.

title: Chosen, not burdened, and He is an excellent Protector.
subtitle: The surah ends: strive, pray, give, hold fast
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}has not given you more than you can bear{/reward}, and cites the Prophet ﷺ: make things easy and do not make them difficult. This is the religion of Ibrahim, whose House the surah began with. Hold fast to Allah, the best Protector and Helper.
now: Some days faith feels like a list you are failing. A missed prayer, a slip, a guilty scroll. {reward}The last verse of the surah says you were chosen, the way is easy, and He is your Protector.{/reward} Start again from there.
old: Religion is a heavy burden I keep failing to carry.
new: I was chosen for an easy, upright way, and Allah Himself is my Protector.
try: Pick one small act of worship you can keep up daily, and begin it today.
